requirements.text: The application must provide a 4-page wizard process for users to apply to withdraw processed payroll.
The wizard must consist of 4 sequential pages: 1. Instructions Page, 2. User Selection Page, 3. Amount Entering Page, and 4. Application Submitted Page.
The Instructions Page must display approximately 100 words of instruction text related to the withdrawal process.
The Instructions Page must feature a button at the bottom, which displays 'Continue application' if an application is already in progress.
Clicking the button on the Instructions Page must redirect the user to the User Selection Page.
The User Selection Page must contain a dropdown list of employees.
Selecting an employee from the dropdown on the User Selection Page must trigger an API call to fetch their details.
The User Selection Page must display the selected employee's full name, email address, department, and salary below the dropdown.
The User Selection Page must have 'Back' and 'Next' buttons at the bottom.
Clicking the 'Back' button on the User Selection Page must redirect the user to the Instructions Page.
Clicking the 'Next' button on the User Selection Page must transition the application status and redirect the user to the Amount Entering Page.
The Amount Entering Page must display the total processed salary amount balance for the selected employee, with already submitted application amounts subtracted.
The Amount Entering Page must contain an input field for the user to enter the desired withdrawal amount.
The Amount Entering Page must display a read-only control showing the remaining balance amount that will be left in the account after the application is submitted.
The Amount Entering Page must have 'Back' and 'Next' buttons at the bottom.
Clicking the 'Back' button on the Amount Entering Page must redirect the user to the User Selection Page.
Clicking the 'Next' button on the Amount Entering Page must transition the application status and redirect the user to the Application Submitted Page.
The Application Submitted Page must display text indicating that the application has been submitted, along with the generated application ID, selected user information, and entered withdrawal amount.
The Application Submitted Page must have a 'Complete application process' button at the bottom.

Clicking the 'Complete application process' button must update the final status of the application, subtract the withdrawal amount from the employee's salary balance, and redirect the user to the home/dashboard page.
A new navigation link named 'applications' must be added to the application navigation menu.
Clicking the 'applications' navigation link must redirect the user to a page containing an application list table.
The application table must display columns for metadata, statusId, created person id, created date, lastchangedate, status last change date, and amount.
The application status must be set to 'Application Created' when the user transitions from the Instructions Page to the User Selection Page.
The application status must be set to 'User Selected' when the user transitions from the User Selection Page to the Amount Entering Page.
The application status must be set to 'Amount Entered' when the user transitions from the Amount Entering Page to the Application Submitted Page.
The application status must be set to 'Application Submitted' when the user completes the wizard on the Application Submitted Page.
A database migration must be created to define the Application table with statusId, created person id, created date, lastchangedate, and status last change date fields.
A database migration must be created to define the Status table and link its ID to the statusId field in the Application table.
The Status table must be seeded with the values: 'Application Created', 'User Selected', 'Amount Entered', and 'Application Submitted'.
A database migration must be created for an Employee Salary Balance table that holds employee ID and their remaining amount balance.
The Employee Salary Balance must be increased and updated whenever payroll is processed for an employee.
The Employee Salary Balance must be decreased by the withdrawn amount upon completion of the application.
The implementation of the payroll withdrawal application process must not affect any existing systems or flows.
